html:
The Battle of Britain was fought in the skies over southern England from 10 July to 31 October 1940. The Royal Air Force beat off the German air force, the Luftwaffe, in the first major battle fought only by aircraft.

After the fall of France, Britain refused to make peace with Germany. Hitler ordered an invasion, which needed control of the air over the Channel. The Luftwaffe had about 2,500 aircraft against some 700 British fighters. But the British had radar stations along the coast, linked by telephone to control rooms that sent Spitfires and Hurricanes where they were needed. In August the Germans bombed airfields and came close to wearing the defence down. On 7 September they switched to bombing London, which gave the airfields time to recover. After heavy German losses on 15 September, Hitler put off the invasion.

Germany lost nearly 2,000 aircraft and Britain about 1,700. The night bombing of cities, the Blitz, went on until May 1941. It was Germany's first defeat of the war. Britain fought on and became the base for the Normandy landings. Churchill said of the pilots that never had so much been owed by so many to so few.
